title: The night Big Sid Catlett died backstage in Chicago
summary: While Stewart was with Tatum at a Chicago theater, Catlett visited backstage in good spirits and collapsed with a stroke during the show.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Now, it was mentioned that you -- were you performing at the place the night that Big Sid Catlett died?
Yes, I was. In fact, I was working, performing with Art Tatum at a theater in Chicago. I forget the name of the theater.

It might have been the Oriental. Well, anyway, we were performing and our friend Sid Catlett came by to see us. He was backstage looking and listening to us while we were performing and I spied him standing backstage, you know, and I kind of waved to him between notes, you know, and it was so good to see him, especially when we took our intermission. We went back and had a good chat with him, you know.
Seemed in good spirits and healthy?

He was in very good spirits and that had been the first time I had seen him since -- had been playing around New York, oh, a couple of years before then, you know. That was the first time that we had seen him, I had

that is, and of course, during our -- we went back on to do our second show and when we came -- when that second show finished, we came off and took our applause and returned and went back and did another number.

Encores and what have you. And all right, the show was finished. So one of the stage hands came up to us and told us what had happened. Sid Catlett had had a stroke of some kind and they took him to the hospital while the show was going on. And I don't know, he probably had died right backstage when we'd seen him a few moments before.
So it just like came out of nowhere.
So when you saw him, he didn't look --
He looked in good health and what have you. Yeah, that was a very sad situation.
